subject: Recap: security & hosting options — proposed path and asks
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: security & hosting options — proposed path and asks

Thanks for the call this morning, Sam — good to meet you and Olivia. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned on the security-driven hosting decision. I’ve put the technical details in Rishi’s inbox for clarity.

High-level summary of LexaCare constraints (from call):
- HIPAA-covered PHI flows will go through the inference path (patient notes, identifiers).
- LexaCare requires an executed BAA, SOC 2 Type II evidence, and audit-log retention for 12 months.
- Prefer data residency in US (no EU hosting requirement at this time).
- Procurement window: target contract signature by end of June; PoC in June if possible.

Options we discussed (short):
1) Hosted API (Redwood public): fastest onboard, can operate under a BAA with tenant isolation and KMS-managed encryption. However, it has multitenant control plane considerations and may require extra safeguards for PHI depending on your risk posture.
2) Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools + VPC peering): good middle ground — predictable throughput, ability to restrict network egress, KMS integration, and fine-grained audit logs. Often the recommended path for teams that want low ops lift but stronger isolation.
3) Private VPC / On-prem: maximum isolation, Redwood control plane with customer-managed networking or on-prem package. Longer lead time and procurement complexity.

Proposed recommendation: start with Dedicated capacity (VPC peering + customer KMS) for the PoC, and run the BAA + SOC2 evidence exchange in parallel. If procurement or risk dictates stricter isolation later, we can roadmap Private deployment.

Asks / next steps:
- Sam / Olivia: confirm procurement and legal point people so we can send the BAA and SOC2 snapshot.
- Rishi: I asked you to prepare a short architecture diagram showing Dedicated + VPC peering + KMS (can we target EOD tomorrow?).
- Monica: draft mutual action plan (timeline for PoC, sign-off criteria, procurement milestones).

Attachments sent with this thread: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2026.pdf (SOC2 snapshot), Redwood_BAA_Draft_LexaCare.docx (BAA draft). Also include a quick schematic for Dedicated (Rishi).

Thanks —
Vivek
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
www.redwoodinference.com

Vivek — thanks for the tidy recap. A few clarifying questions from my side before we loop in procurement: 

1) Encryption and key control: for Dedicated, will LexaCare be able to bring our own KMS (AWS KMS customer-managed keys) and have keys never exportable to Redwood?
2) Audit logs: can you confirm the retention and format for all inference request logs (token-level logs not required, but request/response metadata, timestamps, actor ids, and redaction options)? We need logs to be immutable and accessible for 12 months.
3) BAA: please send the draft to legal (Olivia cc’d) and flag any clauses you expect Redwood to negotiate.
4) STIG/Secure baseline: do you provide a secure-hardened image/architecture for Dedicated and any references for penetration testing?

If Dedicated satisfies (1) and (2) we prefer that approach for the PoC. Timeline-wise procurement will prioritize vendors that can provide an executed BAA + SOC2 evidence within 2 weeks.

Vivek / Monica — quick technical notes to answer Sam’s questions and to prepare the diagram.

1) KMS / keys: Dedicated capacity supports customer-managed KMS keys via AWS KMS (BYOK). Keys are used to encrypt model weights at rest and customer data encryption at rest; they are never exported in plaintext to Redwood. We can document the KMS ARN and key policy required for peering + EBS volumes.

2) Audit logs: request metadata (request id, timestamp, model, route, client id, redaction tag, and status) are available via our audit-log API and can be exported to CloudWatch / S3 (recommended) for immutable retention. We can sign an export retention SLA for 12 months and provide an export job that writes gzipped JSON to your S3. We do not keep full token-level transcripts by default for PHI workloads unless explicitly configured as part of the PoC.

3) Network isolation: Dedicated supports VPC peering and strict egress controls; Private VPC adds customer-managed control plane if you need that. For PoC, VPC peering + security groups + restricted NAT should be sufficient.

4) Pen test / baseline: we can share our pentest summary and the secure-hardened AMI checklist. We maintain an internal compliance pack (SOC2 auditor report) — attached the SOC2 snapshot and an internal pentest sprint summary (redacted).

I’ll attach a quick diagram (deployment-architecture-dedicated-vpc.png) and a short technical checklist for procurement. If Legal wants any specific KMS language, ping me and I’ll provide recommended text.

-Rishi
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

Sam / Olivia — following up with a concrete proposal based on our conversation and Rishi’s notes.

Recommended path for PoC: Dedicated capacity with VPC peering + BYOK (AWS KMS) and audit-log export to LexaCare S3 (12-month retention). This gives the isolation and proof points you need while keeping time-to-PoC fast.

Mutual action plan (high level):
- This week: sign and return the attached BAA draft (Redwood_BAA_Draft_LexaCare.docx) to loop legal. I flagged standard PHI language — we can iterate on any line items.
- By 12 May: set up initial VPC peering and KMS handshake; Rishi will schedule a 90-minute technical onboarding call with your infra team.
- By 20 May: provision Dedicated instances for PoC and run sample workloads (we’ll agree on a small prompt set for quality and latency checks).
- By end of June: procurement target for contract signature (deal LEX-2027-0423).

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2026.pdf (SOC2 snapshot), Redwood_BAA_Draft_LexaCare.docx, deployment-architecture-dedicated-vpc.png.

Links: HubSpot deal HS-34721, DocuSign pre-fill (linked below).

If that timeline works I’ll set up the legal + procurement cadence with Olivia and schedule Rishi’s onboarding slot.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this quickly.
